data.summary: This directory is a declarative installation fragment for the `zoxide` shell tool (a smart `cd` replacement) within a larger aio-config / devcontainer image-generation setup. It pairs a `scenario.toml` metadata file that declares the scenario id, category, installer (mise) and pinned version with a `fragment.Dockerfile` that performs the actual idempotent mise-based install and verification. Together they let the generator resolve, order and compose this tool layer with other mise fragments in the Docker build.

file_insights.name: fragment.Dockerfile
file_insights.summary: Docker build fragment that installs zoxide via `mise use -g` at a templated version and verifies the binary is resolvable in both login and non-login shells.
file_insights.source_summary: A single ARG + RUN pair. ARG ZOXIDE_VERSION={{version}} parameterizes the version; the RUN chains `mise use -g "zoxide@${ZOXIDE_VERSION}"`, `mise ls zoxide`, and two `bash` login/non-login existence checks that echo MISSING and exit 1 on failure. Comments explain that zoxide's binary keeps its canonical name (unlike Debian batcat/fdfind renames) and why per-fragment mise config merging is order-independent.
file_insights.detailed_description: This is a small, self-contained Dockerfile layer emitted into the final image build. It takes the version from the `{{version}}` placeholder (filled in by the aio-config generator from scenario.toml), runs `mise use -g zoxide@<version>`, lists installed tools, and then asserts that `command -v zoxide` succeeds under both `bash -lc` and `bash -c` to catch PATH problems in interactive vs non-interactive shells. Because `mise use -g` reads/merges/writes the config, the fragment is idempotent and can be composed with other mise tool fragments in any Docker layer order without an aggregation step.
responsibilities: Parameterize the zoxide version via build ARG
Install zoxide globally through the mise aqua backend
Verify installation by listing mise tools
Assert the `zoxide` binary is on PATH for both login and non-login bash shells

file_insights.name: scenario.toml
file_insights.summary: Scenario metadata consumed by `aio-config gen` that declares the zoxide scenario id, description, shell category, mise installer and the single pinned version 0.10.0.
file_insights.source_summary: Declarative TOML only: an id/name/description/category/installer header plus a single `[[versions]]` table with label and version both set to "0.10.0". No executable logic; comments point at the sibling fragment.Dockerfile as the file holding the install steps.
file_insights.detailed_description: This TOML file is the machine-readable contract between the scenario and the aio-config fragment resolver. It identifies the scenario (`id = "zoxide"`), gives human-facing metadata (name, Chinese description of the smart-cd behavior), classifies it under `category = "shell"`, and states that installation is performed by `installer = "mise"` using the aqua backend into /opt/mise/installs. Its `[[versions]]` array supplies the version values that get substituted into the neighboring fragment.Dockerfile placeholder.
responsibilities: Declare the unique scenario id and display metadata
Specify the installer (mise) and shell category for resolution/ordering
Provide the pinned version list (0.10.0) used to fill the Dockerfile ARG placeholder
